title: Lab Normal Ranges & Critical Values
body:
> **Key:** Every range below is a typical adult reference range. **Reference and critical values vary by lab, assay and patient age.** The number that matters is the one printed on your own facility's report. Critical values require a documented read-back callback.

## CBC

| Test | Adult range | Typical critical |
|---|---|---|
| WBC | `4.5–11.0 x10^3/microL` | under `2.0` or over `30` |
| Hemoglobin | M `13.5–17.5 g/dL`, F `12.0–16.0` | under `7.0` or over `20` |
| Hematocrit | M `41–53%`, F `36–46%` | under `20%` or over `60%` |
| Platelets | `150–400 x10^3/microL` | under `50` or over `1000` |
| MCV | `80–100 fL` | — |
| Neutrophils | `40–70%` | ANC under `500` = severe neutropenia |
| Lymphocytes | `20–40%` | — |

## BMP / CMP

| Test | Adult range | Typical critical |
|---|---|---|
| Sodium | `135–145 mEq/L` | under `120` or over `160` |
| Potassium | `3.5–5.0 mEq/L` | under `2.5` or over `6.5` |
| Chloride | `98–107 mEq/L` | — |
| CO2 (bicarbonate) | `22–29 mEq/L` | under `10` or over `40` |
| BUN | `7–20 mg/dL` | over `100` |
| Creatinine | `0.6–1.2 mg/dL` | over `5` or a rapid rise |
| Glucose | fasting `70–99 mg/dL` | under `50` or over `450` |
| Calcium (total) | `8.5–10.5 mg/dL` | under `6.5` or over `13` |
| Ionized calcium | `1.1–1.3 mmol/L` | — |
| Magnesium | `1.7–2.2 mg/dL` | under `1.0` or over `4.7` |
| Phosphate | `2.5–4.5 mg/dL` | under `1.0` |
| Albumin | `3.5–5.0 g/dL` | — |
| Total bilirubin | `0.3–1.2 mg/dL` | — |
| AST / ALT | `10–40` / `7–56 U/L` | — |
| Alkaline phosphatase | `44–147 U/L` | — |

**Anion gap** = `Na − (Cl + HCO3)`. Normal `8–12 mEq/L`. If potassium is included (`Na + K − (Cl + HCO3)`) normal runs `10–20`. A gap over `12` sends you to MUDPILES.

## Coagulation

| Test | Range | Critical |
|---|---|---|
| PT | `11–13.5 s` | — |
| INR | `0.8–1.1`; warfarin target `2.0–3.0` (`2.5–3.5` mechanical mitral valve) | over `5.0` |
| aPTT | `25–35 s`; heparin therapeutic `60–90 s` | over `100 s` |
| Fibrinogen | `200–400 mg/dL` | under `100` |
| D-dimer | under `0.50 mcg/mL FEU` | — |

## Cardiac and perfusion markers

| Test | Range | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| High-sensitivity troponin | assay-specific, commonly under `14 ng/L` | Serial draw at `0` and `1–2 h`; the **delta** matters more than one value. Sex-specific cutoffs are standard |
| Conventional troponin I | under `0.04 ng/mL` | Rises `3–4 h`, peaks `12–24 h`, stays up `7–10 d` |
| CK-MB | `0–5 ng/mL` | Largely retired in favor of troponin |
| BNP | under `100 pg/mL` | over `400` makes heart failure likely |
| NT-proBNP | under `125 pg/mL` (under age `75`) | Age-adjusted cutoffs |
| Lactate | `0.5–2.0 mmol/L` | over `2` concerning; `4.0` or more triggers the sepsis bundle and is a callback at most labs |

## ABG and VBG

| Value | ABG | VBG (approx) | Critical |
|---|---|---|---|
| pH | `7.35–7.45` | `7.31–7.41` | under `7.20` or over `7.60` |
| PCO2 | `35–45 mmHg` | `41–51 mmHg` | under `20` or over `70` |
| PO2 | `80–100 mmHg` | `30–40 mmHg` (useless for oxygenation) | under `55` |
| HCO3 | `22–26 mEq/L` | same | — |
| Base excess | `−2` to `+2` | same | — |
| SaO2 | `95–100%` | — | under `88%` |

## Urinalysis

| Item | Normal |
|---|---|
| Color / clarity | Yellow, clear |
| Specific gravity | `1.005–1.030` |
| pH | `4.5–8.0` |
| Protein, glucose, ketones, blood, bilirubin | Negative |
| Leukocyte esterase, nitrite | Negative |
| Urobilinogen | `0.2–1.0 mg/dL` |
| WBC | `0–5 /hpf` |
| RBC | `0–3 /hpf` |
| Bacteria, casts | None to rare |

## Other common sends

| Test | Range | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Lipase | `10–140 U/L` | Pancreatitis usually at least `3x` the upper limit |
| Amylase | `30–110 U/L` | Less specific than lipase |
| Ammonia | `15–45 mcg/dL` (`11–32 micromol/L`) | On ice, to the lab now. Critical over `100` |
| TSH | `0.4–4.0 mIU/L` | Free T4 `0.8–1.8 ng/dL` |
| HbA1c | under `5.7%` normal; `5.7–6.4%` prediabetes; `6.5%` or more diabetes | Most treatment targets sit under `7%` |

## The rule of 3

For a normal, non-anemic adult: `RBC x 3 = Hgb`, and `Hgb x 3 = Hct`. So `4 : 12 : 36` or `5 : 15 : 45`. A set that badly violates the rule usually means a dilutional draw, a clotted tube or a real hemoglobinopathy — look at the specimen before you believe the number.

## Four-step ABG

1. **pH** — under `7.35` acidemia, over `7.45` alkalemia. This names the primary problem.
2. **PCO2** — the respiratory number. In a respiratory problem it moves *opposite* the pH.
3. **HCO3** — the metabolic number. In a metabolic problem it moves the *same* direction as the pH.
4. **Compensation** — other value normal is uncompensated; both abnormal with an abnormal pH is partially compensated; both abnormal with a normal pH is fully compensated (use which side of `7.40` the pH sits on to name the primary).

ROME: **R**espiratory **O**pposite, **M**etabolic **E**qual. Then read oxygenation (`PaO2`, `SaO2`) as a separate question.
